name: Sámi and Finno-Ugric peoples of the north
summary: The Sámi of northern Scandinavia and the Finno-Ugric peoples of the northern forests, such as the Khanty, Mansi and Komi, who lived by hunting, fishing and reindeer herding.

knownFor.label: Joik
knownFor.note: A Sámi song form that “sings” a person, animal or place.

knownFor.label: Reindeer herding
knownFor.note: Herding reindeer for meat, milk, hides and transport.

location.value: Finno-Ugric languages are spoken in Eastern, Central and Northern Europe and North Asia; Sápmi is the northern part of the Fennoscandian Peninsula.

terrain.value: Taiga forest, tundra, lakes and rivers.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

climate.value: Long, cold winters and short summers.
climate.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

resources.value: Reindeer, fish, fur animals and forests.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

disasters.value: Hard winters and poor hunting years.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

population.value: The four largest groups: Hungarians (14.5 million), Finns (6.5 million), Estonians (1.1 million) and Mordvins (0.85 million).

urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

disease.value: Epidemics after contact with farming peoples.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

migration.value: Finnish and Estonian ancestors moved west to the Baltic; Hungarians’ ancestors moved to Central Europe (9th century).
migration.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

economicBase.value: Hunting, fishing, trapping and reindeer herding.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

tradeRoutes.value: Traded furs with Norse, Novgorod and Volga Bulgar merchants.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

wealth.value: Wealth was counted in reindeer and furs.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

moneyAndTax.value: Paid fur tribute to Norse, Novgorod and later Russian rulers.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

inequality.value: Mostly equal communities, apart from owners of large herds.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

governmentType.value: No state; the article covers language groups and their Russian republics (Karelia, Komi, Udmurtia, Mordovia, Mari El, Khanty-Mansi).

keyRulers.value: No kings were recorded; leaders were elders and family heads.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

succession.value: Elders and family heads guided communities.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

institutions.value: The siida system shared hunting and grazing lands.
institutions.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

stability.value: Moved with the seasons and the herds.
stability.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

territoryChange.value: Lands taken over gradually by Scandinavian and Russian states.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

alliancesRivals.value: Traded with neighbours such as Norse, Slavs and Karelians.
alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

inventions.value: Skis (some of the oldest known skis come from this region), sleds, fish traps.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

scienceEducation.value: Oral knowledge, with shamans (noaidi) as keepers of tradition.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

openness.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

communicationTransport.value: Skis and reindeer sleds in winter, boats in summer.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

religion.value: Nature spirits and shamanism; Christianity from the 17th–18th centuries.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

languageWriting.value: Sámi and other Uralic languages (related to Finnish, Estonian and Hungarian).
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

dailyLife.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people

colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Finno-Ugric peoples; Wikipedia: Sámi people
